## Question flow (6e)

> **Superseded twice over.** Doc 26 cuts these ten questions to six and resequences the flow behind the first logged meal, so its inventory wins over the table below. And the numeric inputs are US units as of 29 Aug 2026: height in feet and inches shown as `5'11"`, weight in pounds, converted to cm and kg by the client before the request. Sections `6f`, `6g` and `6h` below are still current.

**One question per screen.** Ten of them, in this order:

| # | Question | Control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | How old are you? | stepper, years |
| 2 | Biological sex | options — Female / Male |
| 3 | How tall are you? | stepper, cm |
| 4 | Current weight | stepper, kg |
| 5 | What are you aiming for? | options — Cut / Maintain / Gain |
| 6 | Goal weight | stepper, kg — **skipped when maintaining** |
| 7 | How fast? | options — Relaxed / Moderate / Aggressive |
| 8 | Activity outside training | options — Sedentary → Very active |
| 9 | Training days per week | stepper, days |
| 10 | Anything you avoid? | free text, optional |

Chrome: `‹ BACK` left, `5 OF 10` right, a 3px accent progress bar, then the question at 30px/800. Footer note: `One question per screen. Going back keeps every answer.`

**Three control types, no more.** Options as full-width rows that fill accent when selected; integers as a 62px accent numeral between two 56px steppers; free text as a single field. A stepper beats a keyboard here for the same reason it does on the review screen — no keyboard covering the value being set, and one-handed.

**Skip logic runs in both directions.** Choosing *Maintain* removes goal weight going forward and going back — a skipped question that reappears on the way back is a classic multi-step bug.

Hints carry the judgement the numbers can't: `A desk job all day is sedentary even if you train hard.` · `Faster is not better. Aggressive cuts cost muscle and adherence.` · `Used for the BMR formula, nothing else.`

All ten answers are collected **before** any AI call. One request, not a conversation.

## ~~Building targets (6f)~~ — cut 31 Aug 2026

**There is no wait to draw.** The AI call went, so target generation is one arithmetic pass on the server and the sixth answer goes straight to the result screen.

The screen existed to fill a few seconds of model latency, and it did a good job of it: three rows explaining that the maths was local and only the judgement was being asked for. That was the honest answer to "why is an LLM doing arithmetic?" The better answer turned out to be not to.

Keep the row copy in mind for E4's photo estimate, which has a real wait and the same need to say what is happening.

The original spec:

| Row | Value | Sub-line |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `MIFFLIN-ST JEOR BASELINE` | `2,180 KCAL` (green, done) | Computed locally. Free, instant, reproducible. |
| `ADJUSTING PROTEIN & FIBER` | `ASKING…` (accent, live) | The baseline goes into the prompt as context, so the model adjusts and explains rather than doing the maths. |
| `CHECKING SERVER BOUNDS` | `QUEUED` (muted) | Anything outside sane limits falls back to the formula. |

## Targets result (6g)

Three numbers as a grouped list, each 40px/900 with its macro's colour on the mono label. Then, in order:

**Baseline line** — `BASELINE 2180 → SET 2150` with `WITHIN SERVER BOUNDS` in green. The guardrail made visible rather than implied.

It survives the 31 Aug 2026 removal of the AI call, with a narrower job. It used to catch a model drifting from the baseline. Now it shows the clamp acting on the formula's own output, which happens at the edges of the supported weight band. Show the line only when the two numbers differ, because `BASELINE 2180 → SET 2180` is noise.

`WHY THESE NUMBERS` — the rationale, in plain language, roughly 60 words. Names the deficit, the rate, why protein is set from body weight, and why fiber matters on a cut.

**Written from a template, not by a model. Changed 31 Aug 2026.** This section used to end: *"This paragraph is the actual value the AI call adds; without it the whole call is a formula with extra steps."* True, and it turned out to be the argument for cutting the call rather than for keeping it. A paragraph about numbers the server just computed does not need a model to write it, and a template reads the real values instead of being told about them:

> 2,180 calories. That is your resting burn of 1,750, times your activity, minus 20% for your goal. Protein at 176 g is 1.0 g per pound, the band research supports for holding muscle in a deficit. Fiber at 32 g follows the US guideline of 14 g per 1,000 calories.

Same length, same job, and it cannot name a figure that is not on the screen. See doc 05.

**Disclaimer**, in an over-target-orange panel, in the flow rather than as a footnote:

> These are estimates, not medical advice. If you're managing a health condition or you're pregnant, talk to a professional before following them.

Non-negotiable for a health-adjacent public app, and Apple review will look for it.

`ACCEPT AND START` (accent) and `ADJUST THEM` (secondary). Never force acceptance of a generated number.

## Adjust (6h)

Heading `Your call`. Three steppers — kcal ±10, protein ±5 g, fiber ±1 g — then two notes.

**Live bounds feedback.** The baseline row turns orange with one of two warnings, rewritten 29 Aug 2026. The original text said `OUTSIDE BOUNDS — SERVER WILL CLAMP` and that the server clamps regardless. It does not, for a value the user typed themselves. Doc 05 carries the full ruling.

Outside the **suggested** range (calories 1,500–3,200; protein 100–260 g in the prototype), the row turns orange with `OUTSIDE THE RANGE WE SUGGEST` and the value saves exactly as typed. A person is allowed to disagree with the app about their own body.

Outside the **absolute** range, calories under 1,000 being the case that matters, the server rejects the write with a `400`. The stepper should not let the user reach it, so this is a backstop rather than a screen anyone should meet.

The distinction is the point. A warning says "we think this is unwise". A refusal says "this is not a target". Silently storing a different number than the one someone typed is worse than either.

**Versioning, stated:**

> Saving writes a new version. Days you've already logged keep the targets that were live at the time — last week's progress never gets rewritten.

Button reads `SAVE NEW VERSION`, not Save. The append-only model from doc 02 is surfaced in the copy, because it is the thing users get wrong assumptions about.

**This screen doubles as the settings target editor.** Same component, different entry point — accepting onboarding targets and editing them later both POST a `TargetVersion`, differing only in `source`.

## Implementation notes

* Steppers clamp at 0 client-side; the server owns real validation
* Question state must survive navigation — a `useReducer` over the whole answer set, not per-screen `useState`
* Response shape validated strictly: request JSON, parse it, reject malformed output. Do not pattern-match prose
* If the model's numbers fall outside bounds, fall back to the deterministic formula **and log it** — that log is how you find out the prompt regressed

## Still to design

Targets history (the list of versions over time — small feature, makes the versioning tangible, genuinely interesting on a long cut), and the failure state for the AI call timing out mid-onboarding.
